title: Deck – Phone Control Panel for Coding Agents
tools: Python (aiohttp) · tmux · Rust (iroh peer-to-peer tunnel) · Android (Capacitor) · Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi
blurb: A small web app running on each PC, allowing a phone to create, monitor, and communicate with LLM coding agents. Each agent operates within a dedicated tmux session, ensuring that work continues even if the phone goes to sleep or loses connection, and the phone receives a notification when an agent completes a task or requires input.
long: Deck runs on each of my PCs (personal computers) and gives my phone a column of tabs, one per session, plus one-tap keys that start Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, agy (Google’s Antigravity CLI, command-line interface), OpenClaw or my own shell scripts. Each one runs in its own tmux session on the PC, so closing the phone or losing signal never stops an agent.

Agents appear as a chat instead of a raw terminal: streamed responses, tappable expandable tool calls, and questions converted to buttons. A bridge process launches each agent in machine readable mode (eg codex app-server, pi --mode rpc) or for Claude, monitors its transcript and uses hooks, and writes a standardized event stream that the page replays. A shelf stores saved responses and documents (PDF, Word, Markdown) that the agents can read. On PC there is a review view that displays a document alongside the chat.

Multiple PCs connect to a single Deck without a primary host: all hosts display all hosts’ sessions in one tab list, and the android app moves to the next host if the host it connects to does not respond within 4s. Chats can migrate between hosts during a conversation. Machine notes are a git repository, each host has a full copy and pushes to other hosts.

To gain access, you need to pair. The deck only listens on localhost, so either use Tailscale or the built-in iroh tunnel (direct encrypted peer-to-peer connections with a relay fallback), and the new device needs to claim a one-time code (which expires after 5 minutes) and the new device needs to be approved from an already paired device. Phone notifications use ntfy.
highlights: Six agent types plus custom scripts, each in its own tmux session
Linked computers with no main host; the phone app fails over after 4 s
